test_cases.title: FW-B0 toolchain proof: firmware workspace host build and test, RP2350 target build, lint gate, sw_gate.sh end to end, and rustos blinky and cwht-app flashed on a bare Pico 2 (dev-board case, supporting evidence)
test_cases.setup: Article: pico2-devboard-1. Credit: false (dev-board run, charter section 3). Credit row: SUPPORT. Purpose: FW-B0 toolchain proof of docs/process/07-software-engineering-plan.md sections 3.1 and 3.2 (test-only module SW-TOOL, docs/process/04-verification-and-validation.md section 1). It shows that the firmware workspace firmware/ (crates cwht-app, cwht-core, cwht-hal-mock of 07 section 1.2) builds and tests on the host, builds for thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf against rustos by path, passes the lint configuration of 07 Annex B, that tools/sw_gate.sh runs end to end, and that a rustos image and the cwht-app image load over the Pico 2 USB bootrom and run. It closes no requirement: REQ-SYS-127 and REQ-SYS-128 close by Inspection (row I) and REQ-SYS-133 by Demonstration on the delivered unit (row D); this case is supporting evidence for all three. Configuration: host is the owner's Mac (macOS 26.6.2, arm64) with the tools and versions of tools/toolchain.lock.md; firmware/rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.98.0, and until that toolchain is installed (owner-approved download) the gate runs on stable only when its rustc --version equals the lock rustc row exactly; rustos at the commit of the lock rustos row, read only; the rustos blinky is built from rustos templates/pico2 copied to a scratch directory with its two git dependency lines replaced by the local path form of rustos templates/README.md; target board a bare Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (RP2350) with nothing connected except its micro-USB cable to the Mac; images loaded with picotool 2.3.0 in BOOTSEL mode. Credentials: tools per tools/toolchain.lock.md at the commit recorded in the report; no tool has a TV record yet, so all output is developer evidence (CM plan section 9.1). Safety: USB-powered 3.3 V logic only, no RF, no cells; handle the board by its edges; unplug the cable before touching the pins. Environment: room temperature 18 to 28 C; indoor lighting in which the on-board LED is plainly visible.
procedure: Record the configuration: git rev-parse HEAD of cwht and of rustos, git status of rustos api/ and firmware/ (must be clean), rustc --version and cargo --version in firmware/, rustup toolchain list, rustup target list --installed, the cargo tool versions (nextest, llvm-cov, audit, deny, geiger) and picotool version, into versions.txt; confirm the rustos commit equals the tools/toolchain.lock.md rustos row and rustc equals its rustc row.
Host build: in firmware/ run cargo build (default members cwht-core and cwht-hal-mock) and record the output in host-build-test.txt.
Host tests: in firmware/ run cargo test and append the output to host-build-test.txt; record the number of tests run and passed.

Target build: in firmware/ run cargo build -p cwht-app --release --target thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf; confirm that the build output carries no compiler or linker warning and that firmware/target/thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf/release/cwht-app.map exists, and record the flash and RAM use that gate G2 computes from the link map and the rustos pico2 link.ld MEMORY regions (included in step 6).

Lint and format: run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --exclude cwht-app --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo clippy -p cwht-app --target thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf -- -D warnings (both included in step 6, gate G1).

Gate: run tools/sw_gate.sh (stops at the first FAIL) and tools/sw_gate.sh --keep-going (runs every step of G1 to G6 past a FAIL; setup and G0 failures stop it in both modes) and record both logs, sw-gate-full.txt and sw-gate-keep-going.txt, with every PASS, FAIL and MISSING line and the exit status.

Gate known-answer runs: run gate-known-answer.sh, which executes tools/sw_gate.sh --quick (--keep-going for KA-8) on nine copies of firmware/ in a scratch directory: KA-0 unmodified, KA-1 an unwrap in cwht-core, KA-2 a formatting defect, KA-3 a failing host test, KA-4 an unsafe block with transmute in cwht-core, KA-5 a lock rustc row that differs from the installed rustc, KA-6 an unwrap in cwht-app, KA-7 a cargo:warning line in cwht-app/build.rs, KA-8 run1-junit.xml and run2-junit.xml left from an earlier invocation in firmware/target/nextest/ together with a failing host test; record exit status and the first FAIL line of each in gate-known-answer.txt.

Fresh rustos blinky: build the copied rustos templates/pico2 with cargo build --release twice into two target directories; record both ELF SHA-256 values and compare them with each other and with the rustos root file blinky.elf in blinky-build.txt.

UF2 conversion: copy the blinky ELF and the step 4 cwht-app ELF into the report directory as rustos-blinky.elf and cwht-app.elf, run picotool uf2 convert <name>.elf <name>.uf2 --family rp2350-arm-s for each and picotool info -a on each UF2; record output and SHA-256 values in uf2-info.txt.

Blink-rate prediction: disassemble both ELFs with rust-objdump -d, count the instructions executed per spin_loop call in each delay loop, and compute the full blink period for a system clock of 4.6 MHz to 19.6 MHz (RP2350 datasheet section 8.3.1, ring oscillator at boot) and 1 to 2 cycles per instruction; record in blink-rate-prediction.txt.

Flash and observe the rustos blinky (owner and Claude): the owner writes 1 on the board if it is unmarked, holds the BOOTSEL button, plugs the micro-USB cable into the Mac, then releases BOOTSEL. Claude runs picotool info -d (the device is listed in BOOTSEL mode), then picotool load -v docs/vv/reports/TC-SW-TOOL-001-r1/rustos-blinky.uf2 and picotool reboot, and records the output. The owner counts complete off-to-on LED transitions for 60 s timed on a stopwatch, reports the count and whether on and off times look equal.

Flash and observe cwht-app (owner and Claude): the owner unplugs the cable, holds BOOTSEL, plugs it in again and releases BOOTSEL. Claude runs picotool info -d, picotool load -v docs/vv/reports/TC-SW-TOOL-001-r1/cwht-app.uf2 and picotool reboot, and records the output. The owner counts complete off-to-on LED transitions for 60 s as in step 11 and reports the count.
Record tool versions, the cwht and rustos commits, the procedure blob and every artifact SHA-256 in the report.
On any discrepancy, stop and open an NCR per docs/process/04-verification-and-validation.md section 10.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Pass if all of the following hold: steps 2 to 4 each exit 0 and every host test of step 3 passes (at least 10 tests); step 5 reports no formatting difference and no clippy warning; tools/sw_gate.sh exits 0 in step 6 (the FW-B0 exit criterion of 07 section 3.2), with the G6 emulation step printing its SKIP line; in step 7 KA-0 exits 0 and KA-1 to KA-7 each exit 1 with the first FAIL line at the gate of the seeded defect (G1 clippy host for KA-1 and KA-4, G1 cargo fmt for KA-2, G3 run 1 for KA-3, G0 for KA-5, G1 clippy target for KA-6, G2 no compiler warning for KA-7), and KA-8 exits 1 with the G3 identical result sets line reporting FAIL; the two blinky builds of step 8 have identical SHA-256; picotool info -a in step 9 reports target chip RP2350 and image type ARM Secure with one image def block for each UF2; in steps 11 and 12 picotool load -v reports the verify passed and picotool reboot exits 0, and the owner counts 10 to 120 LED cycles in 60 s for the rustos blinky and 3 to 45 LED cycles in 60 s for cwht-app (the step 10 prediction windows, 13 to 114 and 5 to 39 cycles in 60 s, widened to round limits). Otherwise Fail; Blocked while a prerequisite is absent. The result is supporting evidence only and changes the status of no requirement.
instruments: Host computer (owner's Mac) USB port supplying the Pico 2 over its micro-USB cable, with picotool 2.3.0 per tools/toolchain.lock.md
Stopwatch (phone clock) for the 60 s blink count; not a credited instrument, this case is credit: false
